children: US corn and soybean futures fell to fresh multi-week lows on Monday as funds liquidated long positions amid active harvesting across the Midwest and forecasts for continued favourable weather this week.
Corn was down for a fifth straight session and soybeans were down for a sixth straight day to lows not seen since August.
Wheat futures followed corn and soybeans lower, shrugging off concerns about Black Sea grain exports amid the ongoing

US farmers are expected to produce their largest-ever soybean crop this year and their second-largest corn crop, and harvesting weather has improved since scattered rain stalled field work in some areas last week.

"We had an absolutely wide-open harvest window over the weekend," said Ted Seifried, chief market strategist at Zaner Ag Hedge. "So we are seeing harvest pressure and, again, funds seem to be liquidating their long positions."

Chicago Board of Trade December corn (CZ26) settled down 7-1/4 cents at $4.67 a bushel, its lowest in nearly 10 weeks. November soybeans (SX26) fell 7-3/4 cents to a 7-1/2 week low of $12.53-1/2 a bushel, as harvest pressure more than offset support from renewed Chinese import demand.

after several daily export "flash sales" announcements last week.

The USDA is due to update its weekly crop progress estimates later on Monday. Analysts polled by Reuters, on average, expect the agency to report the corn harvest at 49% complete and the soy harvest at 66% done.
CBOT December wheat (WZ26) was down 5-1/4 cents at $6.55-1/4 a bushel, its lowest since August 12.
Russian wheat export prices declined slightly last week while analysts raised October export forecasts as shipments disrupted by the war with Ukraine are being redirected to Baltic terminals.
